text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- The price of medicines will go up by 12 percent on average as of January 15, said Elemer Kiss, spokesman of the Prime Minister's Office. Owners of energy companies will be allowed to sell their stakes any time. Hungarians will be allowed to exchange an unlimited amount of foreign currency for tourism purposes from January 1. @

- Joining the European Union is vital for Hungary, but the process will demand serious sacrifices both on the part of society and the economy, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told the Top 100 conference of representatives of the country's leading companies yesterday. Hans van den Broek, European Commissioner for external relations stressed that the reforms must continue.
- Although economic growth will probably begin in Hungary next year, the public finance deficit is likely to increase from this year's 4.1 to 5.3 percent of GDP, warns an OECD report. @

- Due to GDP growth and lower inflation expected for 1997, next year may see a decrease in the crawling peg devaluation of the forint, central bank president Gyorgy Suranyi said, adding that inflation may drop to 17 per cent by December 1997.

- Yesterday Parliament passed a law on the Hungarian News Agency MTI, an amendment to the privatisation law, and a bill to allow taxpayers to voluntarily devote one percent of their personal income tax toward "public purposes".
- The financial services company Co-Nexus will be wound up without a legal successor. @
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. together with the finance and industry ministries believe that the truck manufacturer Raba should be privatised on the stock exchange.
- OTP Bank will receive a 10-year, $50 milion subordinated loan from EBRD.
- The Budapest City Council yesterday approved the nomination of Nograd County Police Chief Attila Berta to the top police post in the nation's capital.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Parliament also passed the 1997 budget of the two social security funds yesterday. @
- A consortium comprising the hotel chain Eravis Rt., Pannon-Valto Rt. and Aquincum Rt. have purchased 50 percent of Hunguest Hotels Rt., an unnamed official of the first investor said.

- The East European Food Fund, managed by the London-based Jupiter Asset Management, and the US-based Advent Private Equity have purchased 38 percent of poultry breeding and processing company Hajdu-Bet Rt.
- Early this week MOL concluded a long-term contract on buying natural gas from the French company Gaz de France. @

- The 51,000th Suzuki rolled off the production line at Esztergom on Wednesday, president and CEO Akira Shinohara announced yesterday when he received the company's ISO 9002 quality certificate. 1996 will be the first profitable year for the company.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will announce today that HUF 5 billion of special funds will be made available in 1997 to replace old police cars and develop information systems at regional police headquarters. @
- A 190-ton shipment of toxic waste which found its way to Hungary eight months ago with false papers was sent back to Germany on Thursday.
